result.title: Instructor-designed AI improves learning in a randomized trial across 19 universities
result.summary: Universities are alarmed by recent evidence that artificial intelligence (AI) can undermine learning, with students prescribed generic chatbots or centrally designed AI tools performing worse. In a pre-registered randomized controlled trial across 7,200 students at 19 universities over three semesters, we tested whether AI designed by frontline instructors can improve learning. We encouraged instructors to design AI solutions they believed would best help their students. Drawing on their unique knowledge of their classes and students, the instructors created a wide array of innovations. We show that these instructor-designed AI innovations improved student learning, measured by AI-proof assessments (proctored, in-person examinations). We found no change in student engagement, measured by course activity records, or satisfaction, measured by course evaluations. Our findings demonstrate that AI can improve student learning when its adoption is frontline-driven, with instructors empowered to design and refine AI solutions for their own classrooms.

AI.brief_summary: 一项在19所大学、7200名学生中开展的预注册随机对照试验，检验由一线教师自行设计 AI 工具能否提升学习成效，结果显示以现场考试衡量的学习成绩提高，参与度与满意度无变化。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究关注教育场景中 AI 工具的设计主体与学习成效，不涉及视觉或多模态推理的内部状态、证据使用或停止决策，也无方法层面的可借鉴线索。
